title: Migrating from climdex.pcic
text: Every ETCCDI 27 index climdex.pcic maps climatekit function. function names mirror canonical ETCCDI codes possible. Beyond ETCCDI 27, climatekit also exposes ET-SCI heatwave family (ck_hwn(), ck_hwf(), ck_hwd(), ck_hwm(), ck_hwa()) cold-wave duals (ck_cwn() etc.), agroclimatic indices (Huglin, Winkler, Branas), drought indices (SPI, SPEI), comfort indices (heat index, humidex, wind chill). ck_etccdi_27() returns audit table maps every ETCCDI code climatekit function one place.

title: Migrating from climdex.pcic
text: Inputs. climdex.pcic builds climdexInput object daily temperature precipitation series runs index functions object. climatekit takes daily numeric vectors Date vector directly. preliminary input object. Outputs. climdex.pcic returns numeric vector indexed year (month). climatekit returns tidy data frame period, value, index, unit columns: tidy shape composes directly rbind(), ggplot2, downstream tabulation. reshaping needed. Reference period. percentile-based indices (ck_tx10p(), ck_tn10p(), ck_tx90p(), ck_tn90p(), ck_r95p(), ck_r99p(), ck_wsdi(), ck_csdi(), ck_hwn() family) use ref_start = 1961L, ref_end = 1990L default. Pass values override: -base bootstrap. climdex.pcic implements Zhang et al. (2005) -base bootstrap remove self-inclusion bias years inside reference period. climatekit implement bootstrap v0.2.0. Years inside reference period therefore show small bias (documented function’s roxygen). climate-change attribution work, restrict interpretation years outside reference window, apply bootstrap externally. Future versions may add . Calendar-day window. packages use 5-day window centred day year percentile estimation, pooled across reference period. Spell-counting conventions. packages use 6 days minimum WSDI / CSDI. climatekit’s ET-SCI heatwave family uses 3 days minimum (min_spell = 3L), matching ET-SCI / climpact.

code: # The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) fits a gamma distribution to # monthly precipitation totals over a rolling window, then transforms to # standard normal deviates. Values below -1 indicate moderate drought, # below -1.5 severe drought, below -2 extreme drought.  dates_long <- seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), as.Date("2024-12-31"), by = "day") set.seed(42) precip <- rgamma(length(dates_long), shape = 2, rate = 0.5)  spi <- ck_spi(precip, dates_long, scale = 3) head(spi) #>       period      value index        unit #>   2015-03-01 -0.2891577   spi dimensionless #>   2015-04-01  0.4458927   spi dimensionless #>   ...  # SPEI adds evapotranspiration to capture temperature-driven drought pet <- ck_pet(tmin, tmax, lat = 51.5, dates = dates)

what: Removing the in-base bias with the Zhang (2005) bootstrap
title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
code: # The percentile-day indices (TX10p, TN10p, TX90p, TN90p) compute # thresholds from a reference period (default 1961-1990). For analysis # years inside the reference period, the year being assessed contributes # to its own threshold and biases the result toward 10% / 90%. Set # bootstrap = TRUE to apply Zhang et al. (2005) leave-one-out resampling # (the canonical climdex.pcic / climpact behaviour). Costs roughly # N^2 percentile fits for an N-year reference; opt in for attribution # work spanning the base.  ck_tx10p(tmax, dates, ref_start = 1961L, ref_end = 1990L, bootstrap = TRUE)

Required inputs daily Tmin Tmax; optional inputs (humidity, wind speed, incoming solar radiation, elevation) increase accuracy. humidity, wind, solar radiation missing, FAO-56 fallback estimators used.

title: Reference Evapotranspiration (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith) — ck_pet_pm
text: tmin Numeric vector daily minimum temperatures (degrees C). tmax Numeric vector daily maximum temperatures (degrees C), length tmin. lat Numeric. Latitude decimal degrees. dates Date vector length tmin. elev Numeric. Elevation sea level metres (default 0). wind Numeric vector single value. 2-m wind speed (m/s). Default 2 (FAO-56 fallback unmeasured wind). rh_min, rh_max Optional numeric vectors daily minimum maximum relative humidity percent. must supplied together; otherwise vapour pressure falls back e0(tmin). rs Optional numeric vector daily incoming solar radiation (MJ m^-2 day^-1). NULL, Hargreaves-Samani estimate used. albedo Numeric. Surface albedo (default 0.23). krs Numeric. Hargreaves-Samani coefficient Rs fallback (default 0.16 inland sites; 0.19 coastal).

title: Reference Evapotranspiration (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith) — ck_pet_pm
text: Inputs units: tmin, tmax: daily minimum maximum temperature (degrees C). lat: latitude decimal degrees, used extraterrestrial-radiation calculation. elev: elevation sea level metres (default 0). wind: 2-metre wind speed (m/s). Default 2 m/s (FAO-56 fallback value wind data unavailable). rh_min, rh_max: minimum maximum daily relative humidity (\ pressure estimated e0(tmin) (FAO-56 Eq. 48). rs: daily incoming solar radiation (MJ m^-2 day^-1). NULL, estimated Hargreaves-Samani: Rs = krs * Ra * sqrt(Tmax - Tmin) krs = 0.16 inland sites. albedo: surface albedo (default 0.23, FAO grass reference).

title: climatekit: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought — climatekit-package
text: Compute standard suite climate indices daily weather observations. Provides canonical 'ETCCDI' 27 (Expert Team Climate Change Detection Indices), 'ET-SCI' heatwave cold-wave families plus Excess Heat Factor Nairn Fawcett (2013), agroclimatic, drought, human-comfort families. Drought indices ('SPI', 'SPEI') accept choice distribution (gamma Pearson III SPI; log-logistic generalised extreme value SPEI). Reference evapotranspiration available via Hargreaves FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method (Allen et al. 1998). Percentile-based indices support Zhang (2005) -base bootstrap. Daily inputs numeric vectors plus 'Date' vector; outputs tidy data frames. Optional gridded support via 'terra' applies index 'SpatRaster' reads 'netCDF' input. external API calls; pairs data packages 'readnoaa'. References: Alexander et al. (2006) doi:10.1029/2005JD006290 ; Zhang et al. (2011) doi:10.1002/wcc.147 ; Zhang et al. (2005) doi:10.1175/JCLI3366.1 .

title: climatekit: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought — climatekit-package
text: Maintainer: Charles Coverdale charlesfcoverdale@gmail.com

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: ck_total_precip() now applies canonical ‘ETCCDI’ ‘PRCPTOT’ wet-day filter (precipitation >= 1 mm) default. Pass wet_day_threshold = 0 recover previous raw-sum behaviour. ck_first_frost() ck_last_frost() gain lat argument use hemisphere-appropriate cutoffs. Southern Hemisphere users longer get silent NA results. ck_branas() gains lat argument; Southern Hemisphere growing season now October-February following year. ck_precip_intensity() (SDII) returns NA periods valid observations rather NaN.

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: ck_tx10p(), ck_tn10p(), ck_tx90p(), ck_tn90p() gain bootstrap = FALSE argument. TRUE, leave-one-resampling Zhang et al. (2005) applied remove self-inclusion bias analysis years inside reference period. canonical ‘climdex.pcic’ / ‘climpact’ behaviour required climate-change attribution work spanning base period.

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: ck_hwm(), ck_hwa(), ck_cwm(), ck_cwa() gain mode = c( "excess", "absolute") argument. "excess" (default) preserves existing ‘ET-SCI’ / ‘climpact’ convention. "absolute" returns mean / peak raw temperature event days, matching Perkins-Alexander (2013). New function ck_ehf() implements Excess Heat Factor Nairn Fawcett (2013), Australian Bureau Meteorology operational heatwave metric. Three annual statistics exposed via stat = c("max", "n_positive", "sum_positive").

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: ck_spi() gains distribution = c("gamma", "pearsonIII"). Pearson III preferred arid regions wet-day distribution highly skewed (Stagge et al. 2015). ck_spei() gains distribution = c("log-logistic", "gev"). GEV fitted via Hosking (1985) L-moments.

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: New function ck_pet_pm() implements FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration (Allen et al. 1998), international standard. Optional inputs include relative humidity, wind speed, incoming solar radiation, elevation; FAO-56 fallbacks used unavailable. ck_pet() remains simpler temperature-Hargreaves estimator.

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: Added 13 new functions completing full canonical ‘ETCCDI’ 27 set: ck_txx(), ck_tnx(), ck_txn(), ck_tnn() (extreme values); ck_tx10p(), ck_tn10p(), ck_tx90p(), ck_tn90p(), ck_r95p(), ck_r99p() (calendar-day percentile base, default reference period 1961-1990); ck_wsdi(), ck_csdi() (proper calendar-day spell duration). ck_growing_season() already ETCCDI-compliant. ck_warm_spell() retained quick series-quantile approximation; documentation now points ck_wsdi() canonical ETCCDI definition.

title: climatekit 0.2.0
text: Added 10 new functions implementing ‘ET-SCI’ heatwave cold-wave families calendar-day percentile base. Heatwave family: ck_hwn(), ck_hwf(), ck_hwd(), ck_hwm(), ck_hwa() (number, frequency, duration, magnitude, amplitude). Cold-wave duals: ck_cwn(), ck_cwf(), ck_cwd(), ck_cwm(), ck_cwa(). ‘CWD’ acronym used ‘ETCCDI’ (Consecutive Wet Days) ‘ET-SCI’ (Cold Wave Duration). ck_cwd() ET-SCI cold-wave version; ck_wet_days() ETCCDI precipitation index. function-level documentation pages cross-reference .

title: climatekit 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-03-23 Initial release. 10 temperature indices: frost days, ice days, summer days, tropical nights, growing season length, heating/cooling/growing degree days, diurnal temperature range, warm spell duration. 8 precipitation indices: consecutive dry/wet days, total precipitation, heavy/heavy precipitation days, max 1-day 5-day precipitation, precipitation intensity (SDII). 3 drought indices: Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), potential evapotranspiration (Hargreaves method). 5 agroclimatic indices: Huglin, Winkler, Branas, first/last frost dates. 4 comfort indices: wind chill, heat index, humidex, fire danger index. Generic dispatcher ck_compute() programmatic index selection. ck_available() ck_metadata() index discovery. ck_convert_temp() temperature unit conversion.
